verses.zh: 因此，我―保罗为你们外邦人作了基督耶稣被囚的，替你们祈祷（此句是照对十四节所加）。
verses.en: For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus[NOTE:1] for the sake of you Gentiles
notes: Several early and significant witnesses, chiefly of the Western group (א* D* F G 365), lack ᾿Ιησοῦ (Iēsou, “Jesus”) here, while most Alexandrian and Byzantine mss (P46 א1 A B C D1 Ψ 33 1175 1505 1739 [1881] 2464 M lat sy bo) have the word. However, because of the Western text’s proclivities to add or delete to the text, seemingly at whim, serious doubts should be attached to the shorter reading. It is strengthened, however, by א’s support. Nevertheless, since both א and D were corrected with the addition of ᾿Ιησοῦ, their testimony might be questioned. Further, in majuscule script the nomina sacra here could have led to missing a word by way of homoioteleuton (cMuiMu). At the same time, in light of the rarity of scribal omissions of nomina sacra (see TCGNT 582, n. 1), a decision for inclusion of the word here must be tentative. NA28 rightly places ᾿Ιησοῦ in brackets.

verses.zh: 谅必你们曾听见　神赐恩给我，将关切你们的职分托付我，
verses.en: if indeed[NOTE:1] you have heard of the stewardship[NOTE:2] of God’s grace that was given to me for you,
notes: If indeed. The author is not doubting whether his audience has heard, but is rather using provocative language (if indeed) to engage his audience in thinking about the magnificence of God’s grace. However, in English translation, the apodosis (“then”-clause) does not come until v. 13, leaving the protasis (“if”-clause) dangling. Eph 3:2-7 constitute one sentence in Greek.
Or “administration,” “dispensation,” “commission.”

verses.zh: 用启示使我知道福音的奥秘，正如我以前略略写过的。
verses.en: that[NOTE:1] by revelation the mystery[NOTE:2] was made known to me, as I wrote before briefly.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “namely, that is.”
Or “divine secret” (see Eph 1:9).
Or “as I wrote above briefly.”sn As I wrote briefly may refer to the author’s brief discussion of the divine secret in 1:9.

verses.zh: 你们念了，就能晓得我深知基督的奥秘。
verses.en: When reading this,[NOTE:1] you will be able to[NOTE:2] understand my insight into the mystery[NOTE:3] of Christ
notes: Grk “which, when reading.”
Grk “you are able to.”
Or “secret.”

verses.zh: 这奥秘在以前的世代没有叫人知道，像如今藉着圣灵启示他的圣使徒和先知一样。
verses.en: (which[NOTE:1] was not disclosed to people[NOTE:2] in former[NOTE:3] generations as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets by[NOTE:4] the Spirit),
notes: Verse 5 is a relative clause, subordinate to the thought of v. 4, but it is also parenthetical, interrupting the thought of vv. 4-6. This has been indicated by the parentheses in the translation.
Grk “the sons of men” (a Semitic idiom referring to human beings, hence, “people”).
Grk “other.”
Or “in.”

verses.zh: 这奥秘就是外邦人在基督耶稣里，藉着福音，得以同为后嗣，同为一体，同蒙应许。
verses.en: namely, that through the gospel[NOTE:1] the Gentiles are fellow heirs, fellow members[NOTE:2] of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus.
notes: The phrase through the gospel is placed last in the sentence in Greek for emphasis. It has been moved forward for clarity.
Grk “and fellow members.”

verses.zh: 我作了这福音的执事，是照　神的恩赐，这恩赐是照他运行的大能赐给我的。
verses.en: I became a servant of this gospel[NOTE:1] according to the gift of God’s grace that was given to me by[NOTE:2] the exercise of his power.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “of which I was made a minister,” “of which I became a servant.”
Grk “according to.”
On the exercise of his power see 1:19-20.

verses.zh: 我本来比众圣徒中最小的还小，然而他还赐我这恩典，叫我把基督那测不透的丰富传给外邦人，
verses.en: To me—less than the least of all the saints[NOTE:1]—this grace was given,[NOTE:2] to proclaim to the Gentiles the unfathomable riches of Christ
notes: In Pauline writings saints means any true believer. Thus for Paul to view himself as less than the least of all the saints is to view himself as the most unworthy object of Christ’s redemption.

The parallel phrases to proclaim and to enlighten which follow indicate why God’s grace was manifested to Paul. Grace was not something just to be received, but to be shared with others (cf. Acts 13:47).

verses.zh: 又使众人都明白，这历代以来隐藏在创造万物之　神里的奥秘是如何安排的，
verses.en: and to enlighten[NOTE:1] everyone about God’s secret plan[NOTE:2]—the mystery that has been hidden for ages[NOTE:3] in God[NOTE:4] who has created all things.
notes: There is a possible causative nuance in the Greek verb, but this is difficult to convey in the translation.

Grk “what is the plan of the mystery.” Earlier the author had used οἰκονομία (oikonomia; here “plan”) to refer to his own “stewardship” (v. 2). But now he is speaking about the content of this mystery, not his own activity in relation to it.
Or “for eternity,” or perhaps “from the Aeons.” Cf. 2:2, 7.

Or perhaps “by God.” It is possible that ἐν (en) plus the dative here indicates agency, that is, that God has performed the action of hiding the mystery. However, this usage of the preposition ἐν is quite rare in the NT, and even though here it does follow a perfect passive verb as in the Classical idiom, it is more likely that a different nuance is intended.

verses.zh: 为要藉着教会使天上执政的、掌权的，现在得知　神百般的智慧。
verses.en: The purpose of this enlightenment is that[NOTE:1] through the church the multifaceted wisdom[NOTE:2] of God should now be disclosed to the rulers and the authorities in the heavenly realms.
notes: Grk “that.” Verse 10 is a subordinate clause to the verb “enlighten” in v. 9.
Or “manifold wisdom,” “wisdom in its rich variety.”

verses.zh: 这是照　神从万世以前，在我们主基督耶稣里所定的旨意。
verses.en: This was according to[NOTE:1] the eternal purpose that he accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord,
notes: Grk “according to.” The verse is a prepositional phrase subordinate to v. 10.

verses.zh: 我们因信耶稣，就在他里面放胆无惧，笃信不疑地来到　神面前。
verses.en: in whom we have boldness and confident access[NOTE:1] to God[NOTE:2] by way of Christ’s[NOTE:3] faithfulness.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “access in confidence.”
The phrase “to God” is not in the text, but is clearly implied by the preceding, “access.”
Grk “his.”

By way of Christ’s faithfulness. Though Paul elsewhere teaches justification by faith, this presupposes that the object of our faith (Christ) is reliable and worthy of such faith.tn Or “to God through faith in him.” A decision is difficult here. Though traditionally translated “faith in Jesus Christ,” an increasing number of NT scholars are arguing that πίστις Χριστοῦ (pistis Christou) and similar phrases in Paul (here and in Rom 3:22, 26; Gal 2:16, 20; 3:22; Phil 3:9) involve a subjective genitive and mean “Christ’s faith” or “Christ’s faithfulness” (cf., e.g., G. Howard, “The ‘Faith of Christ’,” ExpTim 85 [1974]: 212-15; R. B. Hays, The Faith of Jesus Christ [SBLDS]; Morna D. Hooker, “Πίστις Χριστοῦ,” NTS 35 [1989]: 321-42). Noteworthy among the arguments for the subjective genitive view is that when πίστις takes a personal genitive it is almost never an objective genitive (cf. Matt 9:2, 22, 29; Mark 2:5; 5:34; 10:52; Luke 5:20; 7:50; 8:25, 48; 17:19; 18:42; 22:32; Rom 1:8; 12; 3:3; 4:5, 12, 16; 1 Cor 2:5; 15:14, 17; 2 Cor 10:15; Phil 2:17; Col 1:4; 2:5; 1 Thess 1:8; 3:2, 5, 10; 2 Thess 1:3; Titus 1:1; Phlm 6; 1 Pet 1:9, 21; 2 Pet 1:5). On the other hand, the objective genitive view has its adherents: A. Hultgren, “The Pistis Christou Formulations in Paul,” NovT 22 (1980): 248-63; J. D. G. Dunn, “Once More, ΠΙΣΤΙΣ ΧΡΙΣΤΟΥ,” SBL Seminar Papers, 1991, 730-44. Most commentaries on Romans and Galatians usually side with the objective view.

verses.zh: 所以，我求你们不要因我为你们所受的患难丧胆，这原是你们的荣耀。
verses.en: For this reason I ask you[NOTE:1] not to lose heart because of what I am suffering for you,[NOTE:2] which[NOTE:3] is your glory.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “I ask.” No direct object is given in Greek, leaving room for the possibility that either “God” (since the verb is often associated with prayer) or “you” is in view.
Grk “my trials on your behalf.”

Which. The antecedent (i.e., the word or concept to which this clause refers back) may be either “what I am suffering for you” or the larger concept of the recipients not losing heart over Paul’s suffering for them. The relative pronoun “which” is attracted to the predicate nominative “glory” in its gender and number (feminine singular), making the antecedent ambiguous. Paul’s suffering for them could be viewed as their glory (cf. Col 1:24 for a parallel) in that his suffering has brought about their salvation, but if so his suffering must be viewed as more than his present imprisonment in Rome; it would be a general description of his ministry overall (cf. 2 Cor 11:23-27). The other option is that the author is implicitly arguing that the believers have continued to have courage in the midst of his trials (as not to lose heart suggests) and that this is their glory. Philippians 1:27-28 offers an interesting parallel: The believers’ courage in the face of adversity is a sign of their salvation.

Or “Or who is your glory?” The relative pronoun ἥτις (hētis), if divided differently, would become ἤ τίς (ē tis). Since there were no word breaks in the earliest mss, either word division is possible. The force of the question would be that for the readers to become discouraged over Paul’s imprisonment would mean that they were no longer trusting in God’s sovereignty.

verses.zh: 因此，我在父面前屈膝，
verses.en: For this reason[NOTE:1] I kneel[NOTE:2] before the Father,[NOTE:3]
notes: For this reason resumes the point begun in v. 1, after a long parenthesis.
Grk “I bend my knees.”

Most Western and Byzantine witnesses, along with a few others (א2 D F G Ψ 0278 1505 1881 2464 M lat sy), have “of our Lord Jesus Christ” after “Father,” but such an edifying phrase cannot explain the rise of the reading that lacks it, especially when the shorter reading is attested by early and significant witnesses such as P46 א* A B C P 6 33 81 365 1175 1739 co Or Hier.

verses.zh: （天上地上的各（或译：全）家，都是从他得名。）
verses.en: from[NOTE:1] whom every family[NOTE:2] in heaven and on earth is named.
notes: Or “by.”
Or “the whole family.”

verses.zh: 求他按着他丰盛的荣耀，藉着他的灵，叫你们心里的力量刚强起来，
verses.en: I pray that[NOTE:1] according to the wealth of his glory he will grant you to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person,
notes: Grk “that.” In Greek v. 16 is a subordinate clause to vv. 14-15.

verses.zh: 使基督因你们的信，住在你们心里，叫你们的爱心有根有基，
verses.en: that Christ will dwell in your hearts through faith, so that, because you have been rooted and grounded in love,

verses.zh: 能以和众圣徒一同明白基督的爱是何等长阔高深，
verses.en: you will be able to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and height and depth,[NOTE:1]
notes: The object of these dimensions is not stated in the text. Interpreters have suggested a variety of referents for this unstated object, including the cross of Christ, the heavenly Jerusalem (which is then sometimes linked to the Church), God’s power, the fullness of salvation given in Christ, the Wisdom of God, and the love of Christ. Of these interpretations, the last two are the most plausible. Associations from Wisdom literature favor the Wisdom of God, but the immediate context favors the love of Christ. For detailed discussion of these interpretive options, see A. T. Lincoln, Ephesians (WBC), 207-13, who ultimately favors the love of Christ.

verses.zh: 并知道这爱是过于人所能测度的，便叫　神一切所充满的，充满了你们。
verses.en: and thus to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, so that you will be filled up to[NOTE:1] all the fullness of God.
notes: Or “with.”

verses.zh: 神能照着运行在我们心里的大力充充足足地成就一切，超过我们所求所想的。
verses.en: Now to him who by the power that is working within us[NOTE:1] is able to do far beyond[NOTE:2] all that we ask or think,
notes: On the power that is working within us see 1:19-20.
Or “infinitely beyond,” “far more abundantly than.”

verses.zh: 但愿他在教会中，并在基督耶稣里，得着荣耀，直到世世代代，永永远远。阿们！
verses.en: to him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS TO 3:1-21

- Considering the theological purpose(s) for the cyclical letter of Paul known as Ephesians, it is
clear that Paul's four main truths in the doctrinal section relate to the Gnostic false teachers.
(See Introduction.)

- Eph. 1:3-4, praises the Father for His "before time" love expressed in Christ's substitutionary atonement
and the Spirit's continuing presence.

- Eph. 1:15-23, Jesus is the true wisdom of God. God wants His people to fully comprehend the gospel (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL).

- Eph. 2:1-10, reveals the Father's great love and mercy for fallen, helpless humanity.

- Eph. 2:11-3:13, reveals the eternal plan of God to include all humans in a free salvation
through Christ (cf. Gen. 3:15), Jew and Greek, male and female, slave and free.

In effect, Eph. 2:11-3:13) reveals the eternal, universal redemptive plan of God (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN; Eph. 2:1-10).
God was fully aware of mankind's rebellion and made plans for dealing with the problem, even
before creation (cf. Eph. 1:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BEGINNING (physical and spiritual)

- Ephesians 2:11-22 and 3:2-13 specify one of several definitions of the mystery of God found in
Paul's writings. Jew and Gentile were united in one new entity, the Church of Jesus Christ.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MYSTERY

- Paul begins a prayer of praise in Eph. 3:1, but gets sidetracked concerning his ministry to the
Gentiles. He resumes his prayer of praise in verses 14-21.

- The prayer which began in verse 1 and finishes in Eph. 3:14-21 divides into three clauses.
(See full note at Eph. 3:16-19)

- believers receive inner strength, Eph. 3:16-17a

- by the Spirit's power

- by Christ's indwelling

- saints may fully comprehend the truth of the gospel and the mystery, Eph. 3:17b-19a

- to grasp so as to hold on to

- to know by experience

- believers are filled with the fullness (plērōma) of God, Eph. 3:19b

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EPHESIANS 3:1-13

1For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the
sake of you Gentiles-2if indeed you have heard of the stewardship of God's grace which was given to me for you;
3that by revelation there was made known to me the mystery, as I wrote before in brief. 4By referring
to this, when you read you can understand my insight into the mystery of Christ, 5which in other generations was not
made known to the sons of men, as it has now been revealed to His holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit; 6to
be specific, that the Gentiles are fellow heirs and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ
Jesus through the gospel, 7of which I was made a minister, according to the gift of God's grace which was given to
me according to the working of His power. 8To me, the very least of all saints, this grace was given, to preach to the
Gentiles the unfathomable riches of Christ, 9and to bring to light what is the administration of the mysterywhich for ages
has been hidden in God who created all things; 10so that the manifold wisdom of God might now be made known
through the church to the rulers and the authorities in the heavenly places. 11This was in accordance
with the eternal purpose which He carried out in Christ Jesus our Lord, 12in whom we have boldness and confident access
through faith in Him. 13Therefore, I ask you not to lose heart at my tribulations on your behalf, for they are your glory.

3:1 "For this reason" Ephesians 3:2-13 is a theological continuation of Eph. 2:11-22. Paul repeats this
phrase in Eph. 3:14, where he returns to his prayer to God. (After a parenthesis of 3:2-13 about his call and
ministry to Gentiles).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of the Gentiles" When Paul wrote this book he was
imprisoned at Rome because of a riot in Jerusalem (see Introduction, Date; cf. Acts 21:27-22:22). The riot occurred
when the Jews accused Paul of taking Trophimus, a Gentile Ephesian convert, into the temple. The Jews knew him to
be a Gentile and were outraged (cf. Eph. 2:14).

Paul felt a specific divine call to minister to the Gentiles (cf. Eph. 3:2,8; Acts 9:15; 22:21; 26:16,18;
Rom. 11:13; 15:16; Gal. 1:16; 2:9; 1 Tim. 2:7; 2 Tim. 4:17).

3:2 "if" This is a FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE which is assumed to be true from
the author's perspective or for his literary purposes. Verses 2-7 form one sentence in Greek. These believers
had heard about Paul's ministry and calling. Paul was not the founder of all the
churches in Asia Minor.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS, VII

▣ "of the stewardship of God's grace which was given to me for you" Paul felt he had been
entrusted with the gospel (cf. Eph. 3:9; 1 Cor. 4:1-2; 9:17; Gal. 2:7; Col. 1:25; 1 Thess. 2:4; 1 Tim. 1:11;
1 Pet. 4:10). God's grace came to Paul as a gift, vv.7-8, and as a stewardship, v. 2 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KOINŌNIA).
This is the twin aspect of God's covenant.

As a matter of fact, all believers have been gifted by the Spirit (cf. 1 Cor. 12:7,11;
Eph. 4:7) and declared stewards of the Great Commission (cf. Matt. 28:19-20; Luke 24:47; Acts 1:8). It is not the
Great Option! It involves both intentional evangelism and Christlike maturity. It is impossible to be a good and
faithful steward and not comprehend the assignment (i.e. 1 Pet. 3:15)!

3:3 "by revelation" This could refer to

- his Damascus road experience (cf. Acts 9:3-8; 22:6-11; 26:12-18)

- Ananias' teachings in Damascus (cf. Acts 9:10-19; 22:12-16)

- the vision in Jerusalem (cf. Acts 22:17)

- Paul's training by the ascended and glorified Jesus in Arabia (cf. Gal. 1:12, 17-18)

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

▣ "the mystery" Paul used the term "mystery" over twenty times with several different meanings.
Often it is associated with the how and why of the union of believing Jews and Gentiles into one new
community, the church (cf. Eph. 2:11-3:13; Col. 1:26-27).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MYSTERY

▣

NASB
"as I wrote before in brief"

NKJV
"(as I wrote before in a few words)"

NRSV
"as I wrote above in a few words"

TEV
"(I have written briefly about this. . .)"

NJB
"as I just described it very shortly"

Peshitta
"as I have briefly written you before"

REB
"I have already written you a brief account of this"

The great reformer, John Calvin, thought this referred to something Paul had written in
a previous letter, but it may better be understood to refer to a previous part of Ephesians,
probably 2:11-22. This common use of the AORIST TENSE is called an EPISTOLARY
AORIST.

3:4 "when you read" This probably refers to the public readings of Paul's letters in the churches
(cf. Col.4:16; 1 Thess. 5:27; Rev.1:3). Remember that Ephesians was a circular letter.

3:5

NASB
"in other generations"

NKJV
"in other ages"

NRSV, REB
"in former generations"

TEV
"in past times"

NJB
"In past generations"

Peshitta
"in ages past"

God is now clearly revealing His age old plan of the redemption of all mankind
(cf. 1 Cor. 2:6-9; Col. 1:26), Jew and Greek, rich and poor, slave and free, male and female (cf.
1 Cor. 12:13; Gal. 3:28).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "was not made known. . .has now been revealed" These are two PASSIVE VERBS,
which show God's actions in the revelation of this great truth

- the Father's will before time (Eph. 1:3-6)

- Jesus' work in time (Eph. 1:7-12)

- the Spirit's work through time (Eph. 1:13-14)

NT believers know more about God, His plan, and His Messiah than any OT person!

▣ "to His holy apostles and prophets" This phrase is also found in Eph. 2:20; 4:11. They are
"holy" because they were set apart for a specific task. This refers to NT prophets (see full note at
Eph. 2:20, cf. Eph. 4:11; Acts 11:27; 13:1; 15:32; 21:9,10; 1 Cor. 12:28; 14:1-40). Both groups, Apostles
and prophets (along with evangelists and pastor/teachers, cf. Eph. 4:11), proclaimed this newly revealed
mystery of the gospel, that believing Jew and Gentile now formed one new body, the church.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (NT)

3:6

NASB
"the Gentiles are fellow-heirs and fellow-members of the body,

and fellow-partakers of the promise"

NKJV
"the Gentiles should be fellow heirs, of the same body,

and fellow-partakers of the promise"

NRSV
"the Gentiles have become fellow heirs, members of the same body,

and sharers in the promise"

TEV
"the Gentiles have a part with the Jews in God's blessings;

they are members of the same body, and share in the promise"

NJB
"pagans now share the same inheritance, that they are parts of the

same body, and that the same promise has been made to them"

REB
"the Gentiles are joint heirs with the Jews, part of the same body

What a startling revelation of the age-old mystery of God's redemptive plan. In Christ
there is no more Jew or Greek (cf. Rom. 2:28-29; 3:22; 10:12; 1 Cor. 12:13; Gal. 3:7-9, 28-29; Col. 3:11).

This same word, "fellow-heirs," is also used in Rom. 8:17; Heb. 11:9 and 1 Pet. 3:7.

There are three sun compounds here:

- "fellow-heirs"

- "fellow members of one body"

- "fellow partakers of the promise"

Paul uses these sun compounds often to describe the believer's new life in Christ. This is
very similar to the three compounds with sun in Eph. 2:5-6.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

3:7 This could refer to Paul's initial salvation, but in context it seems to refer to God's special
gift of his apostolic Gentile mission (cf. Eph. 3:2; 6:20; Rom. 12:3; 15:15-16; 1 Cor. 3:10; 15:10;
Gal. 2:9; Col. 1:25).

▣ "a minister" We get the English word "deacon" from this generic Greek VERB for
minister (diakoneō, cf. Matt. 8:15 or diakonia, cf. Eph. 4:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEACON

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEACONESS

▣ "according to the working of His power" Salvation and effective ministry are of God, not Paul
(cf. Eph. 1:19; Col. 1:29).

3:8-12 This is one Greek sentence. These long sentences are characteristic of Ephesians.

3:8 "the very least of all saints" This is literally "most least," which is a COMPARATIVE
of a SUPERLATIVE (cf. 1 Cor. 15:9; 1 Tim. 1:15). Paul was humbled by his previous life of
religious self-righteousness, and aggressive persecution. He was also amazed by God's love for such a
persecutor of His church.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SAINTS

▣

NASB, REB
"unfathomable"

NKJV, Peshitta
"unsearchable"

NRSV
"boundless"

TEV, NJB
"infinite"

What a powerful word to describe God's riches in Christ (cf. Rom. 11:33 and the Septuagint
translation of Job 5:9; 9:10). Mankind cannot discover God, but God has chosen to reveal Himself.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

▣ "riches of Christ" "Riches" is one of Paul's favorite words (cf. Eph. 1:7,18; 2:4,7; 3:8,16).
In chapter 1 he spoke of the riches of God the Father. Here Paul transfers them to the Son! NT authors
often allude to Jesus' deity by transferring to Him the titles and functions of YHWH (for example see
"God our Savior" and "Christ Jesus our Savior" in Titus 1:3 and 1:4; 2:10 and 2:13; 3:4 and 3:6).

3:9

NASB
"to bring to light"

NKJV
"to make all people see"

NRSV
"to make everyone see"

TEV
"to make all men see"

- In 1 Pet. 1:6 it refers to the manifold sufferings.

- In 1 Pet. 4:10 it refers to the manifold graces of God.

This great multi-faceted truth of God can best be seen in Paul's doxologies in Rom. 11:33-36 and Eph. 3:18-21.

▣ "be made known" The angels longed to know God's plan (cf. 1 Pet. 1:12). God used His love for
the Church to reveal Himself to mankind and to angels (cf. Eph. 2:7; 1 Cor. 4:9).

▣ "the church" Ekklēsia was used in the Septuagint (LXX) to translate the Hebrew
term "assembly (qahal) of Israel" (cf. Exod. 12:6; 16:3; Num. 20:4; Lev. 4:13). This is one of
several uses of this term in Ephesians (cf. Eph. 1:22; 3:10, 21; 5:23, 24, 25, 27, 29, 32). Paul calls the
church the body of Christ both in Eph. 1:22-23 and in Colossians 1:24. The early church saw itself as the
true covenant people of God (cf. Gal. 6:16; 1 Pet. 2:5,9; Rev. 1:6) with Christ Jesus the Messiah as Head.

One of the unusual literary relationships between Ephesians and Colossians is that in
Ephesians this term refers to the church universal (cf. Matt. 16:18; Gal. 1:13), while in Colossians it
refers to the local church (1 Cor. 10:32; 12:28; 15:9; Gal. 1:12; Phil. 3:6). This points toward Ephesians as a circular letter.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklēsia)

▣ "to the rulers and the authorities" This refers to angelic levels of authority, both good and
evil (cf. Rom. 8:38-39; 1 Cor. 2:8; Eph. 1:21; 6:12; Col. 1:16; 2:10, 15, 20). This was a major theological
aspect of Gnosticism. For them, salvation was the procurement of secret knowledge so that one could pass
through these angelic levels (aeons) to reach the high, good god.

A full list of the terms used in the NT for these angelic levels can be seen in George E.
Ladd's A Theology of the New Testament, p. 401. These orders and ranks of angelic beings are not
defined and discussed in detail anywhere in the NT. Be careful of curiosity and systems of theology that
attempt to definitively answer that which the NT leaves ambiguous!

A good example of this caution relates to these angelic ranks. In some passages, they are not
evil but possibly structures of this fallen world which enable humans to live apart from God. A good book
on this theory would be Hendrik Berkhoff's Christ and the Powers, Herald Press.

(epouranious) "in the heavenly places" is only used in Ephesians (cf. Eph. 1:20; 2:6; 3:10; 6:12).
From the context of all of its usages, it must mean the spiritual realm in which believers live here and now,
not heaven.

3:11 "eternal purposes" This is literally "purpose of ages" (cf. Eph. 1:9-10). This term is used in
the Greek Classics to refer to a set plan. God is not surprised and He has no plan B (Luke 22:22; Acts 2:23;
3:18; 4:28)!

What was God's eternal plan? This is clarified in Genesis 1-2. God created mankind for
fellowship (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8); that fellowship was broken by human rebellion (cf. Genesis 3). The
restoration of God's image and fellowship with mankind (Jew and Gentile) is the goal of God's activity in
the Bible. This goal is met through the work of Christ (cf. Gen. 3:15) and the ministry of the Spirit
(cf. John 16:8-14).

The Reformation emphasis on "the priesthood of the believer" was a reaction to the
authoritarian approach of the Catholic Church. However, biblically, the focus is never on the individual believer, but
on "believers" (cf. Exod. 19:6). Western Christianity has magnified the individual to the exclusion of the corporate body.
Christians are to be priests in an evangelistic and corporate sense, not an individual privileged position.
It is true that humans become believers individually, but Christianity is a corporate experience.

3:14 "For this reason" Paul returns to his initial purpose (cf. Eph. 3:1, i.e. his prayer). Notice the
doctrinal section opens with a prayer to the Triune God (cf. Eph. 1:3-14) and closes with prayer. Often in

▣ "I bow my knees" Standing, not bowing, was the usual position for Jewish prayer. See full list

the emphasis on the Father, as in Eph. 1:3-14 (cf. 1 Cor. 15:24-28). The Creator God is the paradigm for all living beings and
their social units (i.e. tribes/nations).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD

3:14-17 "Father. . .Spirit. . .Christ" Notice the work of the Trinity as in Eph. 1:3-14. It is true
that the term "Trinity" is not used in the NT. However, there are numerous passages where the three divine
persons are mentioned in a unified context (cf. Matt. 3:16-17; 28:19; John 14:26; Acts 2:33-34,38-39;
Rom. 1:4-5; 5:15; 8:9-10; 1 Cor. 12:4-6; 2 Cor. 1:21-22; 13:14; Gal. 4:4-6; Eph. 1:3-14, 17; 2:18; 3:14-17;
4:4-6; 2 Thess. 2:13; Titus 3:4-6; 1 Pet. 1:2; Jude 1:20-21).

The KJV translation adds "the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ," but this phrase is not in the
ancient Greek manuscripts P46, א, A, B, C, nor the Greek texts
used by Jerome and Augustine. The addition does occur in the uncial manuscripts
אc, D, G, K, and the Greek text used by Chrysostom. The
UBS4 gives its omission a "B" rating.

The concept of three divine persons with one divine essence (i.e. monotheism) is difficult
to understand. Yet, if Jesus is deity and the Spirit is a person, then Bible believers are forced to affirm a
triune unity.

- Eph. 3:19, "you to know"

This paragraph reflects Paul's prayer for the believers in all these churches that they be stable

- the false teachers

grace of God in Christ (cf. Eph. 1:7,18; 2:4,7; 3:8,16). God's nature is the key to God's power and

▣ "in the inner man" Spiritual growth is internal, but it is stimulated by external pressure.
Paul often uses the contrast between the inner man and the outer man. The inner man is the spiritual aspect,
while the outer man is the physical aspect. The inner man is already part of the New Age, the kingdom of God,
but the outer man is still dying and struggling with the old age, the old fallen nature, and the fallen world
system (cf. Eph. 2:1-3).

3:17 "so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith" This is an AORIST ACTIVE
INFINITIVE which points toward a specific act of faith. There is a fluidity in the NT between the
indwelling of the Son and the Spirit. The Spirit's task (cf. John 14-16) is to

- reveal the need for Jesus (i.e. human sin)

- reveal Jesus (i.e. the gospel)

- draw to Jesus

- baptize into Jesus (cf. 1 Cor. 12:13)

- form Jesus in believers (i.e. Christlikeness)

▣ "being rooted" This is a PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE which could be
translated "have been and continue to be rooted by God." Paul uses this agricultural imagery only here and
in Col. 2:7. These two PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLES are a way of showing his confidence in
these believers and these churches.

▣ "and grounded" This is a second PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE. This is
construction imagery. The same mixing of agriculture and construction imagery is found in Eph. 2:20-22
and 1 Cor. 3:9.

3:18-19 "to comprehend. . .to know" These are both AORIST INFINITIVE (i.e. there are
four AORIST INFINITIVES in this prayer, Eph. 3:16-19). This emphasis on knowledge counteracted
the exclusive claims of the Gnostic false teachers. It may refer to the newly revealed mystery
of God, the uniting of Jews and Gentiles in Christ (cf. Eph. 3:9).

3:18 "may be able" This is the second PURPOSE CLAUSE. Paul is praying that all believers
be strengthened and enabled to fully understand the gospel (i.e. "comprehend" and "know," cf. Eph. 1:15-23).

▣ "with all the saints" This term is always PLURAL, except in Phil. 4:21, which
also has a corporate context. To be a Christian is to be in community. Also, notice that God's will is the
maturity of all believers (cf. Eph. 4:13).

and Body, the Church (cf. Eph. 1:23), His blood-bought, Spirit-filled people!

The term "church" is from two Greek terms, "out of" and "to call." It was used in Greco-Roman
culture for town meetings (cf. Acts 19:32). In Jewish life this term was used to translate the significant
theological concepts of "the assembly of Israel" or qahal (cf. Exod. 12:6; 16:3; Lev. 4:13; Num. 14:5;
20:6; Deut. 5:22; 9:10; 10:4; 18:16). The early believers saw themselves as the true and ongoing "People of
God" (cf. Gal. 6:16; 1 Pet. 2:5-9; Rev. 1:6).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How did Paul learn his theology?

- Why does Paul call himself "the least of the saints"?

- Why was the mystery of God hidden in ages past?

- What is the purpose of the church to the angelic realm?

- List the three things Paul asked God to grant the believers in Eph. 3:16-19.

- What does it mean that Christians are indwelt?
